description: We are aspiring team of high schoolers from Wrocław, who would like to take up the challange and create creative project inwolving our STEM skills.
summary: We developed an educational game meant for kids ages 7 - 12, focusing on conducting research as an astronaut on a mission in the harsh environment of Mars, and at the same time performing scientific research. The player has to think strategically and weigh their decisions carefully in order to maximize their gain, not only through risk taking, but also through collaboration between players. Our game is meant to spark a curiosity in space and STEM in children, as well as introduce them to risk taking at a young age.
details:
HOW DOES IT WORK: Our game’s mechanics are mostly decision-based. They involve choosing a location for field research and making immediate changes . Every round is equivalent to one day on a mission, consisting of three possible moves, where the player can move to one of the available locations, to gather either regular data or promising data tokens, the latter having a higher probability of securing a point. After one round, players have to end up back in base to process and analyse gathered data, i.e. converting collected tokens to points. If an event forces the player to stay outside the base at night, then their first move in the next round is reserved for token evaluation. Analyzing the data might be hard even for a skilled scientist, that means each player must roll dice (if for normal data point d6, if for promising data d8) to determine whether they get a point. Research points are represented by a flipped token.

BENEFITS: Our project can be transformed into a mobile game (for tablets and phones), in order to appeal to mobile fans. For example, parents who would rather install the game on a tablet, instead of buying a physical one to educate their children. 

IMPACT: We want to inspire kids to develop interests in space and STEM through play. We hope to create a similar spark to what we have experienced in our formative years, that eventually brought us to participating in this competition.

TOOLS: In order to create this demo we used digital graphics tools such as: Procreate, Canva, Inkpad and Inkscape. The game board, as well as the card art was hand drawn in Procreate, and icons were created by hand in vector graphics software and then cleaned up by AI tools such as ChatGPT and Claude. Mechanics were fully invented by us, tested in a form of basic prototype with small use of Gemini. 

We have also created simulations of the game in a Python shell, and separately visualized the potential interface of a mobile version in Unity, with an exemplary scene transition using C#. 

CREATIVITY: In order to bring our project to completion we had to get creative, we had to consider the abilities of each of our team members and how to use them to our advantage. Mixing different artistic techniques in our project’s visual language, as well as using the programming skills of our team members to bring our game to life. The game mechanics showcased in our demo were created completely from the ground up and made to be unlike anything else on the market.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED: As a factor we mostly considered the ability to perform the research, yet as a further development we plan to make more factors to consider: like weather, equipment, conditions of base. The same as with new locations and scientists, so as to resemble large teams on research missions, thus potentially the same as it would be on a Mars mission. Those expansions would lead to further development of the scoring system. However, one further development which would be optional and attractive for curious children, a small “lorebook” where some of the topics could  be briefly discussed (eg. Astrobiology is a science which explores…)
